problem.summary: 现有最先进的物体检测网络依赖于区域提议算法来假设物体位置。尽管SPPnet和Fast R-CNN等进展减少了检测网络的运行时间，但区域提议计算成为瓶颈。

motivation.summary: 区域提议计算是测试时计算瓶颈。现有方法（如Selective Search）在CPU上运行，与GPU上的检测网络不匹配，导致运行时间不均衡。需要一种能与检测网络共享卷积特征、近乎无成本的区域提议方法。

core_idea.summary: 引入区域提议网络（RPN），它与检测网络共享全图卷积特征，从而实现近乎无成本的区域提议。RPN是一个全卷积网络，同时预测每个位置的对象边界和对象性分数。RPN与Fast R-CNN合并为一个单一网络，通过共享卷积特征，RPN组件告诉统一网络“看哪里”。

method.summary: 提出Faster R-CNN框架，包含两个模块：区域提议网络（RPN）和Fast R-CNN检测器。RPN在卷积特征图上滑动一个小网络，为每个位置预测多个尺度和长宽比的锚框（anchor boxes）的边界框回归和对象性分数。RPN与Fast R-CNN共享卷积层，通过交替训练或近似联合训练进行端到端训练。

experiments.summary: 在PASCAL VOC 2007、2012和MS COCO数据集上进行了广泛实验。评估了检测精度（mAP）、运行时间、不同锚框设置、λ值敏感性、召回率与IoU重叠比、一阶段与两阶段检测对比等。在ILSVRC和COCO 2015竞赛中，Faster R-CNN和RPN是多个赛道第一名的基础。

claims.claim: RPN与检测网络共享卷积特征，使区域提议几乎无成本。
Faster R-CNN在VGG-16模型上达到5fps的帧率（包括所有步骤），同时在PASCAL VOC和MS COCO数据集上实现最先进的物体检测精度。
RPN生成的区域提议质量高，仅需300个提议即可达到竞争性精度。
两阶段级联（区域提议+物体检测）优于一阶段检测方法。
使用多尺度和长宽比的锚框是有效的回归参考方案。

limitations.limitation: 论文未明确讨论局限性，但可推断：1) 对于非常小的物体，性能可能受限；2) 锚框设计需要针对特定数据集调整；3) 训练过程需要交替训练，可能增加训练时间；4) 在非常深的网络上，实时性（5fps）可能仍不够快。

nodes.title: 输入图像
nodes.label: Input Image
nodes.summary: 输入到整个Faster R-CNN系统的原始图像。
nodes.description: 输入图像首先通过共享的卷积层提取特征图。

nodes.title: 共享卷积层
nodes.label: Shared Conv Layers
nodes.summary: 用于提取图像特征的卷积层，由RPN和Fast R-CNN检测器共享。
nodes.description: 使用ZF或VGG-16等预训练网络作为骨干网络，提取全图卷积特征图。这些特征图被RPN和后续的Fast R-CNN共享，避免了重复计算。

nodes.title: 区域提议网络 (RPN)
nodes.label: Region Proposal Network (RPN)
nodes.summary: 一个全卷积网络，在共享特征图上滑动，为每个位置预测多个锚框的边界框和对象性分数。
nodes.description: RPN在特征图的每个滑动窗口位置，使用一个小的卷积网络（如3x3卷积）映射到一个低维特征，然后通过两个并行的1x1卷积层分别进行分类（cls）和回归（reg）。它为每个位置预测k个锚框（默认k=9，对应3种尺度和3种长宽比）的边界框偏移和对象性分数。

nodes.title: 锚框 (Anchors)
nodes.label: Anchors
nodes.summary: 在特征图每个位置定义的、具有多种尺度和长宽比的参考框。
nodes.description: 锚框是RPN进行边界框回归的参考。默认使用3种尺度（128^2, 256^2, 512^2像素）和3种长宽比（1:1, 1:2, 2:1），共9个锚框。它们构成了一个“回归参考金字塔”，避免了图像或滤波器金字塔的计算。

nodes.title: RPN损失函数
nodes.label: RPN Loss
nodes.summary: 用于训练RPN的多任务损失函数，结合分类损失和回归损失。
nodes.description: 损失函数为：L({pi}, {ti}) = (1/Ncls) * Σ_i Lcls(pi, p*i) + λ * (1/Nreg) * Σ_i p*i * Lreg(ti, t*i)。其中Lcls是分类损失（对数损失），Lreg是回归损失（平滑L1损失），p*i是标签（正样本为1，负样本为0），λ是平衡参数（默认为10）。

nodes.title: 区域提议 (Proposals)
nodes.label: Region Proposals
nodes.summary: RPN生成的候选物体区域，用于后续的检测。
nodes.description: RPN输出一组区域提议（边界框和对象性分数）。通过非极大值抑制（NMS）去除冗余框，保留前N个（如300个）提议作为Fast R-CNN的输入。

nodes.title: Fast R-CNN 检测器
nodes.label: Fast R-CNN Detector
nodes.summary: 基于区域提议的物体检测器，对每个提议区域进行分类和边界框精修。
nodes.description: Fast R-CNN接收RPN生成的区域提议，使用RoI池化层从共享特征图中提取固定大小的特征，然后通过全连接层进行分类（cls）和边界框回归（reg），输出最终的检测结果。

nodes.title: 检测结果
nodes.label: Detection Results
nodes.summary: 最终输出的物体类别和精确边界框。
nodes.description: Fast R-CNN输出每个提议的类别标签和精修后的边界框坐标，以及置信度分数。

deltas.before: 区域提议由外部算法（如Selective Search）在CPU上生成，与检测网络分离，成为计算瓶颈。
deltas.after: 区域提议由RPN在GPU上与检测网络共享卷积特征生成，几乎无额外成本。
deltas.why_it_matters: 消除了区域提议的计算瓶颈，使整个检测系统能够端到端训练并达到近实时速度。

deltas.before: 处理多尺度物体通常需要图像金字塔或滤波器金字塔，计算成本高。
deltas.after: 引入锚框（anchors）作为多尺度和长宽比的回归参考，仅需单尺度图像和特征图。
deltas.why_it_matters: 避免了枚举多尺度图像或滤波器，显著提高了运行效率，同时保持了良好的检测精度。

deltas.before: 区域提议和物体检测是两个独立的模块，无法联合优化。
deltas.after: RPN和Fast R-CNN通过共享卷积特征合并为一个统一网络，可以进行交替训练或近似联合训练。
deltas.why_it_matters: 实现了端到端的训练，可能提升整体性能，并简化了系统流程。

deltas.before: Fast R-CNN使用约2000个区域提议进行检测。
deltas.after: Faster R-CNN仅使用300个RPN生成的提议即可达到竞争性甚至更高的精度。
deltas.why_it_matters: 减少了后续检测阶段需要处理的区域数量，进一步提升了检测速度。

formulas.formula: L({p_i}, {t_i}) = \frac{1}{N_{cls}} \sum_i L_{cls}(p_i, p^*_i) + \lambda \frac{1}{N_{reg}} \sum_i p^*_i L_{reg}(t_i, t^*_i)

variables.name: p_i
variables.description: 锚框i是物体的预测概率

variables.name: p^*_i
variables.description: 锚框i的真实标签（正样本为1，负样本为0）

variables.name: t_i
variables.description: 锚框i的预测边界框参数化坐标

variables.name: t^*_i
variables.description: 与正锚框对应的真实边界框的参数化坐标

variables.name: N_{cls}
variables.description: 分类损失的归一化因子（小批量大小，如256）

variables.name: N_{reg}
variables.description: 回归损失的归一化因子（锚框位置数量）

variables.name: \lambda
variables.description: 平衡分类和回归损失的权重参数（默认为10）

formulas.intuition: RPN的训练目标是一个多任务损失，同时优化锚框的分类（是否为物体）和回归（边界框位置）。分类损失确保模型区分前景和背景，回归损失使预测框更接近真实框。λ用于平衡两个任务的重要性。

formulas.formula: t_x = (x - x_a)/w_a, \quad t_y = (y - y_a)/h_a, \quad t_w = \log(w/w_a), \quad t_h = \log(h/h_a)

variables.name: x, y, w, h
variables.description: 预测边界框的中心坐标、宽度和高度

variables.name: x_a, y_a, w_a, h_a
variables.description: 锚框的中心坐标、宽度和高度

variables.name: t_x, t_y, t_w, t_h
variables.description: 参数化的边界框回归目标

formulas.intuition: 边界框回归的参数化方式。模型预测的是相对于锚框的偏移量（中心点偏移和宽高的对数尺度缩放），而不是绝对坐标。这使得回归目标更易于学习。

main_result.description: 在PASCAL VOC 2007测试集上，使用VGG-16和共享特征的Faster R-CNN达到69.9% mAP，仅使用300个提议。
在PASCAL VOC 2012测试集上，使用VGG-16和共享特征的Faster R-CNN达到70.4% mAP（使用07++12数据训练）。
在MS COCO test-dev上，Faster R-CNN达到42.1% mAP@0.5和21.5% mAP@[.5, .95]。
运行时间：使用VGG-16，整个系统（包括RPN和Fast R-CNN）在K40 GPU上每张图像198ms，帧率5fps。

ablation.description: 锚框设置：使用3种尺度和3种长宽比（69.9% mAP）优于单尺度单长宽比（65.8% mAP）。
λ值敏感性：λ在1到100范围内变化时，mAP变化仅约1%（69.9% vs 67.2%）。
RPN组件作用：移除cls层（无NMS/排序）导致mAP大幅下降（44.6% @100 proposals）；移除reg层（仅用锚框）导致mAP下降（52.1% @300 proposals）。
特征共享：共享特征（69.9% mAP）优于不共享特征（68.5% mAP）。

robustness.description: 在不同数据集（VOC 2007, 2012, COCO）和不同训练数据规模下，Faster R-CNN均表现出一致的性能提升。
使用COCO数据预训练再微调VOC数据，显著提升VOC上的性能（78.8% mAP on VOC 2007）。

scaling.description: 使用更强大的骨干网络（VGG-16 vs ZF）提升检测精度（69.9% vs 59.9% on VOC 2007）。
使用更多训练数据（07+12 vs 07）提升精度（73.2% vs 69.9% on VOC 2007）。

metadata.abstract: State-of-the-art object detection networks depend on region proposal algorithms to hypothesize object locations. Advances like SPPnet and Fast R-CNN have reduced the running time of these detection networks, exposing region proposal computation as a bottleneck. In this work, we introduce a Region Proposal Network (RPN) that shares full-image convolutional features with the detection network, thus enabling nearly cost-free region proposals. An RPN is a fully convolutional network that simultaneously predicts object bounds and objectness scores at each position. The RPN is trained end-to-end to generate high-quality region proposals, which are used by Fast R-CNN for detection. We further merge RPN and Fast R-CNN into a single network by sharing their convolutional features---using the recently popular terminology of neural networks with 'attention' mechanisms, the RPN component tells the unified network where to look. For the very deep VGG-16 model, our detection system has a frame rate of 5fps (including all steps) on a GPU, while achieving state-of-the-art object detection accuracy on PASCAL VOC 2007, 2012, and MS COCO datasets with only 300 proposals per image. In ILSVRC and COCO 2015 competitions, Faster R-CNN and RPN are the foundations of the 1st-place winning entries in several tracks. Code has been made publicly available

Shaoqing Ren, Kaiming He, Ross Girshick, and Jian Sun

Abstract—State-of-the-art object detection networks depend on region proposal algorithms to hypothesize object locations. Advances like SPPnet [1] and Fast R-CNN [2] have reduced the running time of these detection networks, exposing region proposal computation as a bottleneck. In this work, we introduce a Region Proposal Network (RPN) that shares full-image convolutional features with the detection network, thus enabling nearly cost-free region proposals. An RPN is a fully convolutional network that simultaneously predicts object bounds and objectness scores at each position. The RPN is trained end-to-end to generate high-quality region proposals, which are used by Fast R-CNN for detection. We further merge RPN and Fast R-CNN
into a single network by sharing their convolutional features—using the recently popular terminology of neural networks with

“attention” mechanisms, the RPN component tells the uniﬁed network where to look. For the very deep VGG-16 model [3], our detection system has a frame rate of 5fps ( including all steps ) on a GPU, while achieving state-of-the-art object detection accuracy on PASCAL VOC 2007, 2012, and MS COCO datasets with only 300 proposals per image. In ILSVRC and COCO 2015 competitions, Faster R-CNN and RPN are the foundations of the 1st-place winning entries in several tracks. Code has been made publicly available. Recent advances in object detection are driven by the success of region proposal methods ( e.g., [4]) and region-based convolutional neural networks (R- CNNs) [5]. Although region-based CNNs were com- putationally expensive as originally developed in [5], their cost has been drastically reduced thanks to shar- ing convolutions across proposals [1], [2]. The latest incarnation, Fast R-CNN [2], achieves near real-time rates using very deep networks [3], when ignoring the time spent on region proposals . Now, proposals are the test-time computational bottleneck in state-of-the-art detection systems. Region proposal methods typically rely on inex- pensive features and economical inference schemes. Selective Search [4], one of the most popular meth- ods, greedily merges superpixels based on engineered low-level features. Our object detection system, called Faster R-CNN, is composed of two modules. The ﬁrst module is a deep fully convolutional network that proposes regions, and the second module is the Fast R-CNN detector [2] that uses the proposed regions. The entire system is a single, uniﬁed network for object detection (Figure 2).
Using the recently popular terminology of neural

(using an image pyramid) may improve accuracy but does not exhibit a good speed-accuracy trade-off [2]. On the re-scaled images, the total stride for both ZF and VGG nets on the last convolutional layer is 16 pixels, and thus is ∼10 pixels on a typical PASCAL
image before resizing (∼500×375). Even such a large

stride provides good results, though accuracy may be further improved with a smaller stride. For anchors, we use 3 scales with box areas of 1282, 2562, and 5122 pixels, and 3 aspect ratios of 1:1, 1:2, and 2:1. These hyper-parameters are not carefully cho- sen for a particular dataset, and we provide ablation experiments on their effects in the next section. As dis- cussed, our solution does not need an image pyramid or ﬁlter pyramid to predict regions of multiple scales, saving considerable running time. Figure 3 (right) shows the capability of our method for a wide range of scales and aspect ratios. Table 1 shows the learned average proposal size for each anchor using the ZF net. We note that our algorithm allows predictions
that are larger than the underlying receptive ﬁeld.

Such predictions are not impossible—one may still roughly infer the extent of an object if only the middle of the object is visible. The anchor boxes that cross image boundaries need to be handled with care. During training, we ignore all cross-boundary anchors so they do not contribute to the loss. For a typical 1000× 600 image, there
will be roughly 20000 ( ≈ 60× 40× 9) anchors in
total. With the cross-boundary anchors ignored, there are about 6000 anchors per image for training. If the boundary-crossing outliers are not ignored in training,
they introduce large, difﬁcult to correct error terms in

the objective, and training does not converge. During testing, however, we still apply the fully convolutional RPN to the entire image. This may generate cross- boundary proposal boxes, which we clip to the image boundary.

The OverFeat paper [9] proposes a detection method that uses regressors and classiﬁers on sliding windows over convolutional feature maps. OverFeat is a one-stage, class-speciﬁc detection pipeline, and ours is a two-stage cascade consisting of class-agnostic pro- posals and class-speciﬁc detections. In OverFeat, the region-wise features come from a sliding window of one aspect ratio over a scale pyramid. These features
are used to simultaneously determine the location and

category of objects. In RPN, the features are from square (3×3) sliding windows and predict proposals relative to anchors with different scales and aspect ratios. In the second stage of our cascade, the region-wise features are adaptively pooled [1], [2] from proposal boxes that more faith- fully cover the features of the regions. We present more results on the Microsoft COCO object detection dataset [12]. This dataset involves 80 object categories. We experiment with the 80k images on the training set, 40k images on the validation set, and 20k images on the test-dev set. There are a few minor changes of our system made
for this dataset. We train our models on an 8-GPU
implementation, and the effective mini-batch size be-

comes 8 for RPN (1 per GPU) and 16 for Fast R-CNN (2 per GPU). The RPN step and Fast R-CNN step are both trained for 240k iterations with a learning rate of 0.003 and then for 80k iterations with 0.0003. We modify the learning rates (starting with 0.003 instead
of 0.001) because the mini-batch size is changed. For

the anchors, we use 3 aspect ratios and 4 scales (adding 642), mainly motivated by handling small objects on this dataset. In addition, in our Fast R-CNN step, the negative samples are deﬁned as those with
a maximum IoU with ground truth in the interval of

[0, 0.5), instead of [0.1, 0.5) used in [1], [2]. We note that in the SPPnet system [1], the negative samples in [0.1, 0.5) are used for network ﬁne-tuning, but the negative samples in [0, 0.5) are still visited in the SVM
step with hard-negative mining. But the Fast R-CNN

4.3 From MS COCO to P ASCAL VOC
Large-scale data is of crucial importance for improv-

ing deep neural networks. Next, we investigate how the MS COCO dataset can help with the detection performance on PASCAL VOC. As a simple baseline, we directly evaluate the COCO detection model on the PASCAL VOC dataset, without ﬁne-tuning on any P ASCAL VOC data . This evaluation is possible because the categories on COCO are a superset of those on PASCAL VOC. The categories that are exclusive on COCO are ignored in
this experiment, and the softmax layer is performed
only on the 20 categories plus background. The mAP under this setting is 76.1% on the PASCAL VOC 2007 test set (Table 12). This result is better than that trained
on VOC07+12 (73.2%) by a good margin, even though

the PASCAL VOC data are not exploited. Then we ﬁne-tune the COCO detection model on the VOC dataset. In this experiment, the COCO model is in place of the ImageNet-pre-trained model (that is used to initialize the network weights), and the Faster R-CNN system is ﬁne-tuned as described in Section 3.2. Doing so leads to 78.8% mAP on the PASCAL VOC 2007 test set. The extra data from the COCO set increases the mAP by 5.6%.
